claims.statement: Open SWE's backend is a LangGraph application that serves five graphs (agent, reviewer, review-scout, chat, scheduler) together with the FastAPI app (openswe.webapp:app); langgraph.json also declares checkpointer and Store TTL policies and loads .env.

make dev starts local PostgreSQL when POSTGRES_URI is not configured, checks that port 2024 is free, then runs `uv run langgraph dev --no-browser --port 2024 --n-jobs-per-worker 10`, serving the graphs and FastAPI app from the full LangGraph runtime.
make run runs `uvicorn openswe.webapp:app --reload --port 8000` without the LangGraph runtime, so actions that create runs require make dev.
make install installs backend development dependencies with `uv sync --extra dev`; the Makefile provides uv-run wrappers for pytest, Ruff lint/format, and ty typechecking over openswe and tests.

The local development manifest targets LangGraph API `>~=0.15.0rc1`, while pyproject.toml constrains langgraph-api to `>=0.15.0rc1,<0.16`; the standalone Docker image uses the 0.15.1 Python 3.14 LangGraph API base.

langgraph.desktop.json is a separate trimmed desktop manifest that exposes only the agent graph, disables the built-in UI, uses a local auth handler with Studio auth disabled, and supplies a local checkpointer factory.
The pnpm workspace includes bridge-client, ui, desktop, cli, and tests/e2e; Turborepo orchestrates package dev, build, typecheck, test, and check tasks.

make web runs the Turbo dashboard development task; Vite proxies backend prefixes to DASHBOARD_API_URL, defaulting to http://localhost:2024, while make dev-ui runs it beside make dev with DASHBOARD_DEV_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000.
Dashboard build, typecheck, test, and check scripts fan out through Turborepo, while root lint uses oxlint and format/format:check use oxfmt directly.
Turborepo caches .output/**, .vercel/output/**, and build/** for builds, and treats DASHBOARD_API_URL, SOURCE_COMMIT, VERCEL, E2E_HARNESS, and VITE_* as cache-affecting build inputs.

The experimental Electron desktop app packages the compiled dashboard and requires users to select a compatible backend rather than defaulting to a maintainer-hosted deployment; new This Mac tasks use a local sandbox bridge that long-polls that backend while earlier loopback-server threads remain temporarily supported.

make install-desktop refuses a dirty working tree, fast-forwards main, then invokes scripts/install_desktop.sh, whereas make install-checkout runs that script against the current checkout without changing Git state.
scripts/install_desktop.sh is macOS-only, requires Node, ditto, uv, Bun, and pnpm or Corepack, builds the desktop package, then stages and swaps it into /Applications or ~/Applications.

scripts/create_sandbox_snapshot.py builds a LangSmith sandbox snapshot from a Docker image using SandboxClient, prints its ID, and directs operators to set it as a workspace base snapshot in the dashboard.

scripts/purge_wakeup_crons.py is a one-time backfill that can dry-run or delete expired one-shot thread_wakeup crons, resolving the deployment URL from --url/LANGGRAPH_URL and the API key from LANGGRAPH_API_KEY/LANGSMITH_API_KEY.

The root Dockerfile builds the standalone production LangGraph API image, not a sandbox image, from langchain/langgraph-api:0.15.1-py3.14; it installs the repository and registers the FastAPI app, five graphs, and checkpointer TTL through environment variables, exposing port 8000.

A standalone backend requires Agent Server backing configuration including DATABASE_URI, REDIS_URI, LANGSMITH_API_KEY, and LANGGRAPH_CLOUD_LICENSE_KEY, plus a public LANGGRAPH_URL, and must not use scale-to-zero hosting because background runs need Redis/Postgres-backed workers to remain available.

ui/Dockerfile is a multi-stage Node 24 build run from the repository root: it uses a frozen filtered pnpm install, builds open-swe-dashboard into a Nitro .output server, runs it as user node on port 8080, and reads the backend it fronts from DASHBOARD_API_URL at runtime.

A separate production dashboard proxies its backend request paths at runtime, preserving original path/query, streamed non-GET bodies, individual Set-Cookie headers, and browser-visible OAuth redirects; it therefore supports a same-origin proxy arrangement when the backend's dashboard URLs and callback are set to the dashboard origin.

The backend can be deployed to LangGraph Platform by connecting the repository and setting the application environment; the platform build attempts to bundle the dashboard and continues backend deployment if that UI build fails.

The production Nitro proxy requires DASHBOARD_API_URL at request time and throws if it is unset rather than falling back to another backend; it proxies the original path/query and handles OAuth redirects manually.

The FastAPI app rejects wildcard DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS because credentialed CORS is enabled, allows the Electron open-swe://app origin, and installs dashboard, plan, workflow, webhook, health, and other integration routers before mounting the dashboard UI.

The backend can serve a dashboard from DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR or an in-repository ui/.output/public build, while declining reserved API and LangGraph paths so its UI catch-all cannot shadow them; DASHBOARD_DEV_SERVER_URL instead enables a same-origin Vite proxy for hot reload.

Dashboard asset and client-router paths must be built with DASHBOARD_BASE_PATH equal to the LangGraph http.mount_prefix; the platform build derives that value from the manifest, while local builds must supply it.

make tunnel requires NGROK_DOMAIN and exposes local port 2024 through an ngrok policy that returns 404 for every path outside /webhooks/*, protecting unauthenticated LangGraph development routes from public exposure.

The root Docker image does not itself build the dashboard; standalone Docker serving needs a prebuilt dashboard or DASHBOARD_STATIC_DIR, whereas the platform manifest performs a best-effort dashboard build and continues backend deployment if it fails.

A deployment using LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop exposes raw LangGraph routes to network clients; it should instead use LangSmith authentication or an authenticated/private network boundary because dashboard sessions and webhook signatures protect only custom routes.
The local Compose service is PostgreSQL 16 bound to 127.0.0.1:5433 with a health check and named open-swe-postgres volume, so local data survives container removal.

Application startup requires the configured database and runs migrations before starting listeners/workers; several legacy Store-to-Postgres imports are attempted during the lifespan but failures are logged without aborting startup.
make migration runs a script that requires a message, finds the highest numbered migration filename, and generates the next Alembic revision chained to all heads.
make swagger writes sorted, indented OpenAPI output from openswe.webapp:app to swagger.json; the development guide distinguishes these custom FastAPI docs from LangGraph runtime endpoints.

make cli requires Bun and builds cli/dist/oswe; its compiled Bun binary embeds a runtime and the CLI uses a long-polling bridge to execute a remote agent's shell and file requests in the caller's current local directory.

scripts/rebuild_transcript_projections.py rebuilds specified threads' transcript read projections from their event logs using POSTGRES_URI without changing attachments, tool outputs, or thread.version; it continues after individual failures and exits nonzero if any failed.
